actions.name: Configuration Inventory
actions.description: Configuration inventory identifies and records the configuration of software and hardware and their components throughout the organization.
actions.reason: Configuration inventory directly supports establishing a secure configuration process by systematically recording and managing hardware/software configurations.

actions.name: Network Node Inventory
actions.description: Network node inventorying identifies and records all the network nodes (hosts, routers, switches, firewalls, etc.) in the organization's architecture.
actions.reason: Network node inventory ensures all physical/digital network components are identified, which is foundational for secure configuration management.

actions.name: Network Vulnerability Assessment
actions.description: Network vulnerability assessment relates all the vulnerabilities of a network's components in the context of their configuration and interdependencies and can also include assessing risk emerging from the network's design as a whole, not just the sum of individual network node or network segment vulnerabilities.
actions.reason: Network vulnerability assessment identifies configuration-related vulnerabilities and risks, directly supporting secure configuration establishment.

actions.name: Network Traffic Policy Mapping
actions.description: Network traffic policy mapping identifies and models the allowed pathways of data at the network, transport, and/or application levels.
actions.reason: Network traffic policy mapping ensures allowed data pathways align with security policies, enforcing secure configuration boundaries.

actions.name: Principle of least privilege
actions.description: Implement robust access control mechanisms, enforce the principle of least privilege, and regularly update and patch systems to close security gaps that could be exploited for privilege escalation.
actions.reason: Principle of least privilege mitigations enforce minimal access rights, directly enhancing secure configuration controls.
